## How they got there
Real Madrid secured the title by beating Borussia Dortmund 2-0 in the final after navigating a path where they outperformed the vast majority of their peers. The team beat the most opponents on Points per game (98% of that season's teams), followed closely by Pass accuracy at 97% and Shots per game at 97%. Their offensive output was equally dominant, with Attacks per game ranking higher than 91% of the league's squads.

## Would the model have picked them?
With a model probability of 32.0%, Real Madrid significantly exceeded the base rate of 12.5% for reaching the final and held the second-highest rank among all knockout teams. This high standing indicates that the model would have selected them, as only the top two ranks guarantee a selection while lower positions classify teams merely as contenders. The expected stage figure of 1.36 places the team nearest to the quarter-finals on the scale where zero represents elimination before that round and four signifies winning the tournament.

## Weak spots
The club's weakest statistical areas were Long passes (% of passes), which beat only 3% of teams, and Distance covered per game (km), where they surpassed just 9%. Although the model marked Down Shots per game with a negative contribution, Real Madrid ranked in the top 97% for this metric. Similarly, while the model assigned a negative value to Long passes, the team's low frequency here was simply a reflection of their playing style rather than a performance deficit.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat drove, propelled, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
